correctness.rationale: All quantifiers and boundary n>=1/n>=2/n>=3 are explicit. Every omitted edge yields exactly one local implication, and each graph-edge assignment corresponds bijectively to an allowed path or closed walk. Direct 8^3 local-triple enumeration gives 64 states and 102 arcs. Reachability/co-reachability leaves the explicit 14-state open automaton, whose only unlimited walks follow one loop or one six-cycle; residue counting gives exactly 2 or 4 nontrivial open solutions, and the only closed components give 1 or 7 cyclic solutions. The bit weights yield all claimed exponents. Standalone direct edge-subset enumeration separately agrees for open n<=6 and cyclic n<=6. Finite experiments supplement, but do not replace, the complete finite-state proof.

value.rationale: The counting paper motivates enumeration beyond extremal counts. This result determines the complete weight distributions for two natural infinite width-two graph families, exhibiting unexpected bounded numbers of proper solutions and a sharp six-divisibility transition under cyclic closure. It provides an explicit nontrivial DIM-less graph class with proper PED sets exactly on one arithmetic progression, and a structural phase classification rather than only a computable algorithm. No new technique beyond finite-state transfer is claimed; the exact structural cutoff is the mathematical contribution.
